From a universal law to a particular calculation

In Section 1.2, the laws for composition of identifications are stated as identifications of functors on animae of inputs. Applying such a law involves a small calculation: substitute the desired inputs, and compare the resulting endpoints with the expressions in the statement one wants to prove. This note makes that procedure explicit.

We use the primitives, terminal category, products, and composition structure of Sections 1.1–1.2, together with the vertical coherence laws where indicated. All categories and functors below are absolute. A family with parameter \(X\) means an ordinary functor from \(X\) into a fixed identification anima. It does not mean a category varying over \(X\).

We write \(\beta \cdot \alpha \) for vertical composition, with \(\alpha \) applied first, and \(u\star \alpha \) and \(\alpha \star r\) for postwhiskering and prewhiskering. For functor composition we retain \(\circ \).

Lifting two projection comparisons

The product axiom specifies an equivalence \[ q_{F,G}\colon (F=G)\iso (\pi _1F=\pi _1G)\times (\pi _2F=\pi _2G) \] for functors \(F,G\colon X\to C\times D\). Its components are postwhiskering with the two projections.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For specified identifications \(a\colon \pi _1F=\pi _1G\) and \(b\colon \pi _2F=\pi _2G\), there is an identification \(\ell \colon F=G\) equipped with identifications \[ \pi _1\star \ell =a,\qquad \pi _2\star \ell =b. \]

Proof idea

Choose the inverse \(q_{F,G}^{-1}\) supplied with the equivalence and put \(\ell =q_{F,G}^{-1}\circ \langle a,b\rangle \). The inverse comparison, the associator, and the left unitor give \[ q_{F,G}\circ \ell =\langle a,b\rangle . \] Postwhisker this comparison with each projection. The product projection comparisons, including those defining the components of \(q_{F,G}\), give the two asserted identifications. Thus the construction supplies the projection computations as well as the lift itself. □

Substitution through pairing and composition

For \(a\colon X\to C\), \(b\colon X\to D\), and \(r\colon R\to X\), the projection comparisons and associator identify the projections of \(\langle a,b\rangle \circ r\) with those of \(\langle a\circ r,b\circ r\rangle \).

Supplementary Lemma 2. There are identifications \[ \langle a,b\rangle \circ r=\langle a\circ r,b\circ r\rangle . \] For families \(\sigma \colon X\to (f=g)\) and \(\tau \colon X\to (g=h)\), there is also an identification \[ (\tau \cdot \sigma )\circ r =(\tau \circ r)\cdot (\sigma \circ r). \] More generally, specified comparisons \(\tau \circ r=\tau '\) and \(\sigma \circ r=\sigma '\) give \[ (\tau \cdot \sigma )\circ r=\tau '\cdot \sigma '. \]

Proof idea

Apply Supplementary Lemma 1 to the two projection comparisons to obtain the pairing formula. Vertical composition of families is defined by composing their pairing with the composition functor \((g=h)\times (f=g)\to (f=h)\). Reassociate, apply the pairing formula, and postwhisker it with this composition functor. For the last assertion, pair the two specified comparisons and apply the same composition functor. □

Keeping the endpoint comparisons

Supplementary Lemma 3. Suppose \(F,G\colon X\to Y\) are equipped with an identification \(\kappa \colon F=G\). Let \(r\colon R\to X\), and suppose that \(F',G'\colon R\to Y\) are equipped with specified identifications \[ l\colon F\circ r=F',\qquad t\colon G\circ r=G'. \] Then there is an identification \(F'=G'\), given by \[ \bigl (t\cdot (\kappa \star r)\bigr )\cdot l^{-1}. \]

Proof idea

The inverse of \(l\) goes from \(F'\) to \(F\circ r\), prewhiskering \(\kappa \) goes from \(F\circ r\) to \(G\circ r\), and \(t\) goes from \(G\circ r\) to \(G'\). Compose these three identifications with the displayed parenthesization. □

Supplementary Corollary 4. For absolute identifications \(\sigma \colon f=g\), \(\tau \colon g=h\), and \(\upsilon \colon h=k\), the universal vertical coherence laws give \[ \mathrm {id}_g\cdot \sigma =\sigma , \qquad \sigma \cdot \mathrm {id}_f=\sigma , \] \[ (\upsilon \cdot \tau )\cdot \sigma =\upsilon \cdot (\tau \cdot \sigma ), \] \[ \sigma ^{-1}\cdot \sigma =\mathrm {id}_f, \qquad \sigma \cdot \sigma ^{-1}=\mathrm {id}_g. \] These are identifications between the displayed absolute objects of identification animae.

Proof idea

For a unit or inverse law, precompose the universal comparison with \(\sigma \colon *\to (f=g)\). Use Supplementary Lemma 2 to compare the substituted composite with the displayed composite. Constants specialize to their specified values using uniqueness of functors to \(*\) and the unitors. For associativity, use the point whose three projections are \(\upsilon ,\tau ,\sigma \), retaining the product projection comparisons at each step. Apply Supplementary Lemma 3 to the resulting comparisons of both endpoints. □

The same procedure works with a functor from any parameter category into the relevant input anima. Each application retains its own endpoint comparisons. No choice of a universal normal form for all expressions is needed for these finite calculations.
